For procurement teams · Mozambique

Notes for procurement and compliance teams in Mozambique

What the 2026 Petroleum and Local Content Laws, IACM’s drone directive and Lei n.º 6/2024 mean when you buy structure mapping, encroachment surveys or drone work in Mozambique, and what to ask any supplier for. A summary of public rules as of 26 September 2026, for orientation; it is not legal advice.

Send tender documents How we work

In short

Four questions every supplier file should answer

Local content

Does the scope fall under the local-content rules for oil and gas, and does the supplier’s structure meet them?

Drone approvals

If the scope includes drone work, which company will fly, and which IACM and Defence authorisations will it obtain for this survey?

Survey data

Who deposits the drone data with the State, who authorises releasing it to you, and who may reproduce the orthophotos?

Imagery and credits

Which imagery the work uses, its capture dates and licence terms, and how open data is credited.

Oil and gas

Local content under the 2026 laws

Mozambique published a new Petroleum Law and a Local Content Law on 3 June 2026. Both took effect on publication.

Lei n.º 8/2026 (Lei do Petróleo)

  • Foreign individuals or companies that provide services to petroleum operations must associate with Mozambican individuals or companies (art. 60(2)), with real economic substance (art. 60(3)) and local preference (art. 60(4)).
  • The Instituto Nacional de Petróleo is the Autoridade Reguladora do Petróleo (art. 37).
  • Resettlement costs fall on the rights holder, after prior consultation (art. 61).

Lei n.º 8/2026, BR I Série n.º 104, 2.º Suplemento

Lei n.º 9/2026 (Lei do Conteúdo Local)

  • Applies to petroleum and gas projects and to the entities that contract with them, which must pass the obligations on to their subcontractors (art. 3).
  • A Local Content Authority keeps the register of suppliers (cadastro de fornecedores).
  • Partnerships need at least 20 per cent of the share capital held by nationals (art. 17(5)), and national bids get a margin of preference.
  • The exclusivity regime (art. 28) reserves the goods and services in Annex II for firms with at least 80 per cent national production factors, at least 20 per cent Mozambican capital and at least 50 per cent of the wage bill paid to Mozambicans. Annex II lists serviços de topografia, alongside land transport, onshore security, catering, banking, legal, insurance and accounting services.
  • Sanctions include fines, contract cancellation and exclusion from tenders. The implementing regulations were due within 90 days; check whether they have been issued.

Lei n.º 9/2026, BR I Série n.º 104, 3.º Suplemento

Where this service sits

AfriScan registers are remote-sensing analyses of structures, cleared ground and change, built from satellite imagery, open building datasets and imagery you supply. They are not topographic, cadastral or statutory surveys. Drone surveying for oil and gas work is closer to topografia and is likely to be treated as such. Each proposal separates the two, so your local-content team can apply the rules to each part.

Drone work

Who may fly, and what each survey needs

IACM issues approvals for corporate and commercial drone operations only to companies registered and domiciled in Mozambique (DOS-09-2018 §8.3.3(a)). Each commercial operation needs a written IACM approval before it flies, registered aircraft with Certificates of Safety and qualified pilots.

Under Lei n.º 6/2024, the survey itself needs the Minister of National Defence’s authorisation (art. 13(1)(b)), and releasing the data to the client needs the authorisation of the systematic-cartography entity (art. 13(2)). The law applies to the client as an entidade utilizadora (art. 2(1)). A recent decree on licensing aerial work reserves it for national operators, as reported by JLA Advogados; whether it reaches drone work is not settled in the sources we checked.

Drone surveys are subject to the permits and authorisations each job requires. Afridrone is working towards the operator approvals Mozambique requires, and every AfriScan proposal with a drone element names the company that will fly it and the authorisations each flight needs.

The client checklist

Eleven points to check with any drone operator before the first flight, from the company’s registration to the data clause in the contract.

Drone law in Mozambique: checklist

Data

Survey data, privacy and imagery licences

Drone data belong to the State

The original data of aerial coverage by private and foreign companies are State property, and after processing the operator deposits the coverage scheme, navigation data, camera calibration certificate, data copies and a processing report (Lei n.º 6/2024, art. 14). Put the deposit and the release authorisation in the contract.

Privacy

Lei n.º 6/2024 protects privacy, image and honour (art. 6). Mozambique has no general data-protection law yet: the Council of Ministers approved a bill on 3 March 2026 and sent it to the Assembleia da República (INTIC); check its progress. Our registers record structures, not people, and carry no names.

Imagery licences and credits

Each proposal names the imagery the work will use and its capture dates. Open data is credited as its licence requires: Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0), Microsoft Building Footprints (CDLA-Permissive-2.0), © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and Copernicus Sentinel. Map-service basemaps are never delivered as survey imagery.

Public and private buyers

Supplier platforms and public procurement

State bodies buy under the public-procurement regulation, and UFSA keeps the single supplier register, the Cadastro Único (Decreto n.º 79/2022, art. 43), which can be consulted free of charge (UFSA).

The large energy buyers run their own supplier platforms, including the Mozambique LNG supplier registration platform, the Rovuma LNG supplier portal through MozUP, and the supplier portals of ENH and EDM. If your process runs through one of them, name it in your request.

What we send for your supplier file

  • A written proposal: scope, method, imagery plan, deliverables and schedule
  • An imagery statement: sources, capture dates, licence terms and credits
  • For any drone element: the company that will fly it and the authorisations each flight needs
  • The data terms: who receives the results, and the Lei n.º 6/2024 deposit and release steps for drone data
  • Sample outputs, and a sample report on request
  • Written answers to your vendor-qualification questionnaire

Reports and deliverables are available in Portuguese or English.

Frequently asked questions

Is satellite structure mapping "serviços de topografia" under the Local Content Law?

Our registers are remote-sensing analyses of structures, not topographic or cadastral surveys, while drone surveying for oil and gas is likely to be treated as topography. Where a scope sits on that line, the proposal says so, so your local-content team can take a view or ask the Local Content Authority.

Can we use drone orthophotos a supplier delivers to us?

Only if the data were released to you with authorisation. Lei n.º 6/2024 binds the users of aerial-survey products as well as operators, makes acquiring and using products of illegal origin an infraction (art. 16(1)(d)), and requires authorisation to reproduce or publish orthophotos (art. 16(1)(c)). Ask for the release authorisation with the delivery.

Can a consultancy commission the work for its own report?

Yes. ESIA, RAP and engineering consultancies commission structure registers, route comparisons and GIS layers for their own reports, delivered in the formats their teams already use and in Portuguese or English.

What do you need from us to prepare a proposal?

The route or boundary file, the province, the widths or zones to report, the date the record must reflect, the deliverables and the deadline. With a tender, send the documents and the portal or format your process uses.

Know what stands inside your right of way, before it becomes a dispute.

Send us your route or site boundary and the distances that matter to you. We reply with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
